headline: US stocks extend gains as semiconductor rebound lifts tech while Brent trades above $91 amid renewed Iran tensions
raw_text:
- S&P 500 (SPY), Dow (DIA), Nasdaq (QQQ), and Russell 2000 (IWM) trade higher, with technology and small-caps leading the advance
- Teradyne (TER), Western Digital (WDC), and Bloom Energy (BE) post strong double-digit gains on semiconductor recovery momentum and positive earnings sentiment
- Nvidia (NVDA) rises after disclosing a stake in Nebius, while Applied Materials (AMAT), Micron (MU), Marvell (MRVL), Intel (INTC), and AMD (AMD) drive the PHLX Semiconductor Index more than 3% higher
- GM (GM) gains after beating Q2 earnings expectations and raising full-year profit guidance on strong SUV demand
- Utz Brands (UTZ) nearly doubles after agreeing to be taken private in a buyout deal
- Sector rotation favors technology and small-caps, while energy faces headwinds despite the broader market strength
- Brent crude (@QA) trades above $91 as geopolitical risks and potential Strait of Hormuz disruptions rise on fresh Iran developments and wider Mideast tensions
- Investors focus on ongoing AI and tech earnings and key upcoming Big Tech results later this week
- Halliburton (HAL) and 3M (MMM) report earnings today, with no major economic data releases steering market direction
